literal: If one behaves without honoring the great ones, it will bring undeparting suffering by those great ones.
translation: If one conducts oneself without respecting great people, it will bring endless, unremovable distress through those very great ones.
modern: பெரியவர்களை மதிக்காமல் நடந்துகொண்டால், அந்தப் பெரியவர்களாலேயே நீங்காத துன்பம் உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the severe consequences of disrespecting or neglecting wise and powerful elders. If a person behaves without due regard or reverence for them, it triggers ruinous distress. This suffering is described as 'pērā', meaning it is permanent and cannot be easily removed or escaped. Crucially, this inescapable ruin is brought about by the power and influence of the very great ones who were offended.
